concepts.title: Ratio and Percentage Recap
concepts.definition: Ratios compare quantities and percentages express fractions per hundred, so converting between them is a matter of scaling: a ratio a : b becomes the percentage a over a plus b times 100, and any per cent becomes a fraction over 100 for further use.
concepts.key_idea: Every ratio hides a percentage: split the whole into parts and scale to hundred.
question_patterns: convert the ratio 3 : 2 into a percentage
express the given per cent as a ratio
what per cent of the mixture is the first ingredient in the ratio a : b
find the percentage of boys in a class with the given ratio
convert 0.45 into a percentage and a ratio
compare two quantities per cent to per cent

solution_steps.action: take the first part over the whole
solution_steps.explain: The whole is a plus b for a two-term ratio.
Multiplying by 100 reads the fraction per cent.

concepts.title: Finding Discounts
concepts.definition: A discount is a cut on the marked price, usually quoted per cent: discount equals rate per cent of marked price, and the selling price is what survives after the cut - marked price minus discount.
concepts.key_idea: Per cent off the marked price: 20 per cent off 500 rupees is 100 rupees off.
question_patterns: find the discount and selling price when the marked price is 1200 at 20 per cent off
the listed price of a shirt is given with a discount - what does the customer pay
find the discount per cent when the marked and selling prices are given
an item marked 750 rupees sells for 600 - find the discount per cent
calculate the discount amount for the given rate
which shop offers the bigger discount per cent

solution_steps.action: take the rate of the marked price
solution_steps.explain: Discount equals rate over 100 times the marked price.
The selling price is what remains.

concepts.title: Sales Tax and Value Added Tax
concepts.definition: Purchases carry sales tax charged as a per cent of the bill: tax equals rate per cent of the price, and the final bill is the price plus this tax, so a 10 per cent tax on 1000 rupees adds 100 rupees.
concepts.key_idea: Add the tax per cent of the price to get the amount actually paid.
question_patterns: find the final bill when 8 per cent sales tax is charged on 2500 rupees
the price of a fan is given - find the total cost including sales tax
calculate the tax amount for the given rate
the total paid is given with the tax rate - find the list price
what does VAT mean for the customer
compute the amount paid for the item including tax

solution_steps.explain: Rate over 100 times the price of the item.
The bill is price plus tax.

concepts.title: Compound Interest
concepts.definition: Compound interest is interest on interest: each year's interest joins the principal, so the amount grows as principal times (1 plus rate over 100) raised to the number of years, and the interest is the amount minus the original principal.
concepts.key_idea: Recompute the base every period: P(1 + r/100) to the power n, minus P, is the interest.
question_patterns: find the compound interest on 8000 rupees at 5 per cent per annum for 2 years
find the amount when interest is compounded annually
in how many years will the sum double at the given rate
compare simple and compound interest for the given data
what sum lent at the given rate gives the stated amount
find the population after growth at the given rate per year using the CI formula

solution_steps.explain: 1 plus rate over 100 raised to time compounds the rate.
The amount is principal times the factor.

concepts.title: Growth and Decay Applications
concepts.definition: The compound interest formula applies wherever change compounds - population growth at 2 per cent a year, value of an item depreciating at 8 per cent a year - with a negative rate shrinking the quantity instead of growing it.
concepts.key_idea: Same formula, different story: growth with a positive rate, decay with a negative one.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh107.txt section 7.6 (applications of compound interest formula)
question_patterns: the population of a town grows at 2 per cent per annum - find it after 2 years
a scooter bought 3 years ago depreciates at 8 per cent - find its present value
find the number of bacteria after the given growth per hour
by what per cent did the value fall over the given years
apply the compound formula to the given growth rate
find the depreciated value of the machine

solution_steps.explain: Growth adds a positive rate; depreciation uses a negative one.
Multiply the initial value by (1 plus or minus rate over 100) to the power of years.
The product is the value after the given period.

worked_examples.question_pattern: The marked price of an item is {marked} rupees with a discount of {rate} per cent. Find the selling price.

solution_template.explain: Rate per cent of the marked price.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find the discount when {marked} rupees item is sold at {rate} per cent off.

solution_template.explain: Discount equals rate over 100 times marked.

worked_examples.question_pattern: An item costs {price} rupees and attracts {rate} per cent sales tax. Find the amount to be paid.

solution_template.explain: The bill is price plus tax.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A purchase of {price} rupees carries {rate} per cent tax. What is the final bill?

solution_template.explain: Tax is the rate per cent of the price.

solution_template.explain: Compound the rate over the years.
